findings.issue: Cape Helles front sat 3-4 km too far east (it ran onto the slopes of Achi Baba, which the Allies never reached) and had only three positions; it now follows the beachhead of 26 Apr, the lines after First and Second Krithia (28 Apr, 8 May), Third Krithia (4 Jun) and the final Gully Ravine-Vineyard-Kereves Dere line (from 13 Jul), held unchanged to the evacuation.

source.title: Map: Helles war zone, Gallipoli 1915, with the final Allied line (Wikimedia Commons)

findings.issue: The Suvla front of 21 Aug ran 4-9 km too far east (into the Anafarta hills and past Kiretch Tepe); redrawn from Liman von Sanders' annotated map: Kiretch Tepe ridge - Kukurtli Pinar - west of Scimitar Hill - Hill 60 - Damakjelik - the Apex - old Anzac line.

source.title: Liman von Sanders' map of the Suvla and Anzac areas with British front lines, Australian War Memorial (Wikimedia Commons)

findings.issue: The Anzac perimeter reached 1 km beyond Quinn's Post and did not touch the coast at either end; redrawn on Walker's Ridge - the Nek - Quinn's - Courtney's - west of Lone Pine - Chatham's Post, and moved east of Lone Pine after its capture on 6-9 Aug.

The August offensive was missing: Suvla landing 6-7 Aug (Chocolate and Green Hills taken 7 Aug), Chunuk Bair held 8-10 Aug then lost, Hill 60 half-taken 21-29 Aug. Keyframes added for 7, 9, 10 and 29 Aug.
The beachheads were never shown as Allied ground (the map coloured Anzac Cove and Helles Ottoman); added two Allied occupied areas (Helles; Anzac and Suvla) that end with the evacuations.
Beachhead fronts lingered ~5 weeks after the evacuations (front fade rule); they now carry an end date: Anzac and Suvla 20 Dec 1915 (last troops left before dawn on 20 Dec), Helles 9 Jan 1916.

The landings arrow ran to 10 Aug and ended behind Ottoman lines east of Krithia; it now marks the Helles landing (25 Apr - 8 May) ending on the beachhead, and separate arrows mark the Anzac landing (25 Apr) and the Suvla Bay landing (6-21 Aug).
Chapter text omitted the Suvla landing and August offensive and the two evacuation dates; rewritten. Chapter box tightened from 4 x 2.7 degrees to show the beachheads, which are only a few km deep.
Static periods (Helles after 13 Jul, Anzac/Suvla after 29 Aug) now carry an unchanged position about every 5 weeks so the checker's 6-week gap rule is met; the lines genuinely did not move.

The Serbian front jumped from the Danube (6 Oct) to a line through Kosovo and Macedonia (25 Oct) with nothing between, so Belgrade (9 Oct), the Bulgarian attack (from 11/14 Oct) and the fall of Skopje (22 Oct) never appeared; added positions on 11, 22 and 26 Oct, 1, 8, 16, 24 and 29 Nov, 4 and 12 Dec.

On 25 Oct the map already gave the Central Powers all of eastern Serbia and the whole Vardar valley down to the Greek border, and on 25 Nov all of Serbia to the Albanian frontier; Niš fell on 5 Nov, Pristina and Mitrovica on 23 Nov, Prizren on 29 Nov, and the French held the Vardar valley from Krivolak to Gevgelija until early December. Occupied areas rebuilt key by key and kept consistent with the front.

The Allied force landed at Salonika on 5 Oct and advanced up the Vardar to Krivolak (20 Oct) and Gradsko (5 Nov), with the British at Kosturino; this bridgehead was missing (Macedonian front first appeared 12 Dec). Added it with positions on 20 Oct, 5 Nov, 22 Nov, 3 Dec and 8 Dec before the existing 12 Dec border line, plus an arrow for the advance.

Occupied Serbia is now drawn as two areas, the Austro-German zone from the north and a new 'Bulgarian-occupied eastern Serbia and Macedonia (1915)' from the east, meeting on a Morava-Toplica-Kosovo line (later the demarcation of the two occupation zones). A single ring could not morph from two separate bridgeheads into one area without Skopje and Krivolak flickering between sides. The Bulgarian area ends on 25 Jan 1916, when the existing whole-Serbia-and-Montenegro key takes over.

Base-map limitation, not fixed here: the Cliopatria state outline puts the Helles tip west of about 26.23 E and all of Suvla Bay in the sea, so the correct front lines there draw slightly offshore and the Allied fill is clipped away (Anzac shows). Claims that need the Ottoman state underneath (Krithia, Sedd el Bahr after the evacuation) are therefore 'front' claims or were dropped; the base outline should be corrected.

source.title: Map: Helles war zone, Gallipoli 1915, with the final Allied line (Wikimedia Commons)

findings.issue: The Bulgarian First Army's drive on Niš (Negotin 25 Oct, Niš 5 Nov) had no arrow; added one.
Chapter text did not mention the dates of the invasion, Belgrade's fall or the failed Allied advance from Salonika; rewritten (3 sentences).

'Austro-Hungarian incursions into Serbia (1914)' had no end and its last ring (15 Dec 1914) lies on Serbian ground beside the Drina mouth, so a sliver stayed 'occupied' through 1915-1918; it now ends on 16 Dec 1914, when the Austro-Hungarians had been driven out.
Bitola's fall is dated 21 Nov (Wikipedia: Bitola) or 4 Dec 1915 (Wikipedia: Battle of Krivolak); the map lets it fall between the 24 Nov and 4 Dec keys and claims avoid that window.

The Serbian front had no position between 16 Dec 1914 and 6 Oct 1915 (checker gap in the Great Retreat chapter); the front really was quiet on the Drina-Sava-Danube, so the 1914 line is repeated on 10 Jun, 22 Jul and 2 Sep 1915.

Peć and Đakovica (Montenegrin since 1913) fell in December 1915 but sources fetched give no reliable day; the 1915 occupation stops at Serbia's border and Montenegro is left to the January 1916 keys (another reviewer's).

Wikipedia's Pirot article says the Bulgarians entered Pirot on 14 Oct 1915, which conflicts with the USMA map showing the Serbian Second Army on that frontier at the end of October; Pirot is occupied by 1 Nov (claim dated 1 Nov).

No battle marker existed for the 1915 Macedonian fighting; added the Battle of Krivolak (21 Oct - 22 Nov; 5,877 Bulgarian and 3,161 French casualties) and the Battle of Kosturino (6-12 Dec; 1,209 British and 1,804 French casualties, Bulgarian losses uncounted).

Known residue: the app resamples each occupied area to 96 points (about 15 km apart here), so Krivolak, 5 km inside the French bridgehead, shows as Bulgarian-held for about 30 Nov - 2 Dec while the rings morph, a few days before the French actually gave it up (positions held to about 3 Dec; evacuation began 26 Nov). Claims are dated outside this window.

gallipoli.text: To open the straits to Russia and knock the Ottoman Empire out of the war, British, French, Australian and New Zealand troops landed at Cape Helles and Anzac Cove on 25 April 1915. Ottoman defenders held them to beachheads a few kilometres deep; a fresh landing at Suvla Bay and the August attack on the Sari Bair ridge failed too. Anzac and Suvla were evacuated on 20 December 1915 and Helles by 9 January 1916.

serbia.text: On 6 October 1915 German and Austro-Hungarian armies crossed the Sava and Danube and took Belgrade on 9 October; from 14 October Bulgaria attacked from the east, cutting the railway to Salonika. A French and British force landed at Salonika and pushed up the Vardar, but was driven back into Greece by 12 December. Cornered in Kosovo, the Serbian army retreated over the Montenegrin and Albanian mountains to the Adriatic; the survivors were shipped to Corfu and later fought on the Salonika front.
